asA: beta reader who typed the command from the referee-guarantees page
iWant: `rcf audit coverage` with no flag to fail the gate on a stub or missing test, and `--mode shallow-any` to be the documented escape valve
soThat: the docs promise 'a stub or stale pointer fails the gate exactly as a missing test does' holds by construction, and my existing `--strict` invocations do not need rewriting
title: US-16101: strict-by-default coverage with a shallow-any opt-out and a legacy --strict alias

acceptanceCriteria.description: The plain `rcf audit coverage` command runs strict (per-AC) mode. On a tree whose ACs are not all covered by resolving TCs, it prints the table and exits 4; on a fully covered tree it exits 0. The default is the same as the legacy `--strict` invocation.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an initialised RCF project with a scaffold AC-101-1 that has no covering TC
acceptanceCriteria.when: `rcf audit coverage` is invoked with no strictness flag

acceptanceCriteria.description: `--mode shallow-any` reports gaps and exits 0. The output's Coverage-mode line reads `shallow-any` and the table renders the same shape as strict mode; the exit code is 0 even on uncovered ACs.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the exit code is 0 and the output includes 'Coverage mode: shallow-any'

acceptanceCriteria.description: Conflicting flags exit 2 with a usage message. Passing `--mode shallow-any --strict` (in either order) is refused before running the audit; the error names both flags. `--mode` with an unknown value (e.g. `lenient`) also exits 2 with a usage message.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the exit code is 2 and stderr matches /--mode shallow-any conflicts with --strict/
